lessons.title: Supervised vs. Unsupervised vs. Reinforcement Learning

slots.practicalActivity: Classify 5 real-world ML systems (a spam filter, a streaming service's recommender, a game-playing agent like AlphaGo, a house-price predictor, and a customer-segmentation tool) as supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement learning, then note for each whether calling its deployed API is a training event or an inference event.
slots.deliverable: A written table mapping the 5 real systems to their learning type plus a training-vs-inference note for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Load a real small dataset (sklearn's load_iris is fine), identify in writing which columns are features and which is the label, then fit two models of very different complexity on it (a plain LogisticRegression and a DecisionTreeClassifier with no depth limit) and compare their real train accuracy against their real test accuracy.
slots.deliverable: A short script printing train vs. test accuracy for an underfit-leaning model and an overfit-leaning model side by side, with a one-line diagnosis of each.

slots.practicalActivity: Construct a confusion matrix by hand from 10 real predictions vs. true labels you write out yourself, then compute accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 by hand, and check your by-hand numbers against sklearn.metrics on the same 10 values.
slots.deliverable: A worked confusion matrix with all 4 metrics calculated by hand and verified against sklearn's computed values.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: load a real small dataset in sklearn, split it, fit one baseline model, and write a one-paragraph diagnosis of whether it is overfitting or underfitting, backed by the real train and test metric numbers you computed.
slots.deliverable: A written diagnosis paragraph backed by real, printed train/test metric numbers from a model you actually fit.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit sklearn's LinearRegression on a real small dataset (e.g. the California housing dataset, or any 2-column CSV with a numeric relationship), then plot the fitted line against the actual data points.
slots.deliverable: A chart showing real data points with the fitted regression line overlaid.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit a LogisticRegression on sklearn's real load_breast_cancer dataset (the same dataset the capstone uses later) and print its predicted probabilities for 5 real rows next to their true labels.
slots.deliverable: Printed real predicted probabilities for 5 samples alongside their true labels, with a note on which ones the model was least confident about.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit a DecisionTreeClassifier and a RandomForestClassifier on the same breast-cancer dataset, compare their real test accuracy, and render the decision tree's top 2 splits using sklearn.tree.plot_tree.
slots.deliverable: A rendered decision-tree diagram plus a real accuracy comparison table for the single tree vs. the forest.

slots.practicalActivity: Fit sklearn's MLPClassifier (a small neural network) on the same breast-cancer dataset and compare its real test accuracy against the logistic regression and random forest results from the previous two slots.
slots.deliverable: A 3-row comparison table (logistic regression, random forest, small neural network) with real accuracy numbers from models you actually fit.

slots.practicalActivity: Implement gradient descent by hand in plain Python/numpy (no sklearn) for a single-variable linear regression, printing the mean-squared-error loss value after each of 20 real update steps.
slots.deliverable: A printed loss-per-iteration log showing the real loss decreasing across at least 20 gradient-descent steps you implemented yourself.

slots.practicalActivity: Split a real dataset into train/validation/test (e.g. 60/20/20) using sklearn's train_test_split twice, then write a short explanation of why the test set must stay untouched until the very final evaluation.
slots.deliverable: Three correctly sized, non-overlapping real splits verified by printed row counts, plus a written explanation of the held-out test rule.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: pick a new real dataset, split it train/val/test, fit at least 2 of this chapter's model types on it, tune one hyperparameter using only the validation set, then report the final test-set score exactly once.
slots.deliverable: A short report showing validation-based tuning followed by a single, final, real test-set score.

slots.practicalActivity: Download a real messy public dataset (e.g. the Titanic passenger dataset) and identify and fix at least 3 real data quality issues in it, such as duplicate rows, inconsistent text casing, or out-of-range values.
slots.deliverable: A before/after cleaned CSV with a written list of the 3 real issues found and how each was fixed.

slots.practicalActivity: On the same real dataset, engineer 2 new features from existing columns — for example extracting a title from a name field, or bucketing a continuous age column into ranges.
slots.deliverable: The dataset with 2 new engineered feature columns and a one-line justification for why each might help a model.

slots.practicalActivity: Identify every column with missing values in the real dataset using pandas' isnull().sum(), then apply two different real strategies (dropping rows vs. imputing with median/mode) and compare the resulting row and column counts.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison of the drop-strategy outcome vs. the impute-strategy outcome, with real counts from both.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply one-hot encoding to a real categorical column (e.g. 'Embarked') with pandas.get_dummies, and label/ordinal encoding to a different real column (e.g. 'Sex') with a manual mapping.
slots.deliverable: The dataset with both encoding types applied, with the real resulting column names printed out.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately introduce a leakage bug by fitting a StandardScaler on the full dataset before splitting, show it inflates test accuracy, then fix it by fitting the scaler only on the training split and show the resulting (lower, honest) accuracy.
slots.deliverable: Two real accuracy numbers side by side — the leaked result and the fixed result — demonstrating the leakage effect on an actual model.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: take a fresh real dataset you haven't used yet and run it end to end through cleaning, feature engineering, missing-data handling, and encoding, explicitly checking each step for leakage risk before any model fitting.
slots.deliverable: A fully preprocessed, leakage-checked real dataset ready for modeling, with a written note explaining each preprocessing decision.

lessons.title: What a Neural Network Really Is

slots.practicalActivity: Implement a single neuron's forward pass by hand in numpy (weighted sum plus bias, then an activation function) on 3 real input vectors you choose, and print the real output for each.
slots.deliverable: A numpy script computing a real forward pass for one neuron on 3 different inputs, with printed outputs.

slots.practicalActivity: Stack 2 numpy layers (input to hidden to output) using ReLU on the hidden layer and sigmoid on the output, run one real input vector through it, and plot sigmoid, ReLU, and tanh side by side.
slots.deliverable: A plotted comparison of the 3 activation functions plus the printed output of a real forward pass through the 2 stacked layers.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a tiny 2-parameter model in PyTorch, call .backward() to get real autograd gradients, print them, then manually work out one of those gradient values by hand using the chain rule and confirm it matches.
slots.deliverable: Printed real autograd gradient values plus a hand-worked chain-rule calculation that matches one of them.

lessons.title: CNNs vs. RNNs vs. Transformers, Conceptually

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short comparison of what CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers are each structurally built to do well, citing one concrete real-world example task for each (image classification, a text/time-series sequence task, and long-range language understanding).
slots.deliverable: A written 3-architecture comparison table with one real example task mapped to each architecture.

slots.practicalActivity: Load a real pretrained transformer with Hugging Face's pipeline (e.g. pipeline('sentiment-analysis')) and run it on 3 original sentences you write, noting the real model name it used and the real output scores.
slots.deliverable: Captured real pipeline output (labels and scores) for 3 original sentences, with the real model name noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: build a tiny 2-layer neural network in PyTorch (nn.Module) from scratch, train it for 10 real epochs on a toy classification dataset (e.g. sklearn's make_moons), and plot the real training-loss curve.
slots.deliverable: A plotted real training-loss curve over 10 epochs for a from-scratch 2-layer PyTorch network.

slots.practicalActivity: Browse the real Hugging Face Hub and use its filters to find 3 real models for 3 different tasks (e.g. text-classification, summarization, image-classification), recording each model's real download count.
slots.deliverable: A written list of 3 real Hub model names, their task, and their real reported download count.

slots.practicalActivity: Load bert-base-uncased with AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained and AutoModel.from_pretrained, run a real sentence through both, and print the real input_ids shape and last_hidden_state shape, then load the same model via pipeline('sentiment-analysis') and compare the two approaches.
slots.deliverable: Printed real tensor shapes from the two-line from_pretrained pattern, plus one real pipeline() prediction on an original sentence.

slots.practicalActivity: Run a pretrained classifier as-is on 5 real examples from a domain you choose, note which ones it gets wrong, and write a one-paragraph decision on whether those real errors justify fine-tuning or just using the model as-is.
slots.deliverable: A written decision memo backed by 5 real as-is predictions and whether each was correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Compare the pretraining task of the Hugging Face model you loaded earlier (e.g. BERT's masked-language-modeling pretraining) against the new task you ran it on, and write how its learned representations transferred.
slots.deliverable: A written transfer-learning explanation grounded in the specific real model you loaded and the specific task you tested it on.

slots.practicalActivity: Read the real model card for a specific model you're considering (e.g. distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english on the Hub), extracting its real intended-use, limitations, and training-data sections.
slots.deliverable: A written summary of that model's real model-card sections: intended use, limitations, and training data.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: pick a real task you care about, search the Hub for a fitting model, choose one based on its real model card and usage stats, load it via pipeline, and run it on 5 original examples relevant to that task.
slots.deliverable: A documented model-choice rationale plus 5 real pipeline predictions on original examples for the chosen task.

slots.practicalActivity: Load sklearn's real load_breast_cancer dataset (569 samples, 30 features), split it 80/20 with stratify=y, fit a StandardScaler on the training data only, train a LogisticRegression baseline (max_iter=5000), and predict on the 114 held-out test rows.
slots.deliverable: A trained LogisticRegression model plus printed real predictions on the 114-row test set compared against the true labels.

slots.practicalActivity: Score the capstone model's real test predictions using sklearn.metrics: overall accuracy, a full confusion matrix, and precision/recall for both the benign and malignant classes.
slots.deliverable: A printed real confusion matrix and classification report for the capstone model's actual test predictions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a portfolio README for the capstone project covering the problem, the dataset, the approach, and the real accuracy/precision/recall numbers you got, then rehearse a 3-minute walkthrough explaining the model's real precision/recall tradeoffs.
slots.deliverable: A README.md capstone writeup containing the real computed metrics, ready to drop into a portfolio repository.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student understands what is actually happening mathematically and structurally under an LLM API call, can fit, evaluate, and correctly preprocess data for classic ML models in scikit-learn, and has loaded, evaluated, and chosen real pretrained Hugging Face models before completing a from-scratch classification capstone with honest, properly evaluated metrics.
